clue.text: For instance, gets rid of diamond, being heartless?

definitions.text: For instance, gets rid of diamond, being heartless?

parts.words: For instance, gets rid of diamond, being heartless?
parts.note: at bridge a player with no hearts left cannot follow a heart lead and so throws away a card of another suit, such as a diamond

explanation.surface: Someone sheds a diamond, apparently with no heart at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' reads as cruel, but at the card table it means holding no hearts, which is exactly when a player throws off a card from another suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing away a useless card when unable to follow suit is the bridge sense of the verb.

clue.text: Start putting one's cards on the table in corrupt deal

definitions.text: Start putting one's cards on the table

indicators.note: something corrupt is spoilt or debased, so the word deal is rearranged into a twisted form

explanation.surface: Someone begins laying bare their position in a crooked transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting one's cards on the table' sounds like confessing, but at bridge the opening card actually goes on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the first card played to a trick is the opening play, which starts the cards going down.

clue.text: Concerns — lots of little ones raised by partners, normally

definitions.meaning: matters of worry or debate, topics under discussion

definitions.text: lots of little ones raised by partners, normally
definitions.meaning: offspring, the children a couple usually bring up

explanation.surface: Worries about the broods couples usually bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of debate are matters at stake; a couple's children are their offspring, an old legal sense.

clue.text: Patience, for example, as funny fellow hunted animals

parts.note: a card is an informal word for a joker or wag
game is wild animals pursued for sport or food

explanation.surface: Patience is likened to a comedian chasing quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the British name for solitaire, a single-player game with a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is one example of a pastime played with a deck, hence a definition by example.

clue.text: People managing without skill name business associates

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: copers are people who manage or get by
art is a skill or knack

explanation.surface: Unskilled managers name their commercial allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense of outside, so the managers wrap round the skill and the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint owners of a firm share in it as fellow members of the enterprise.

clue.text: Nothing old foursome raised for player taking bow

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the pieces read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a score
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old foursome lifts its game to nothing for a performer taking a curtain call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking bow' suggests applause; the instrument literally takes a bow across its strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The stringed instrument is the 'player' in an orchestra, played with a bow.

clue.text: One hoping trick will work, actually being taken in by French

indicators.note: the Latin phrase is held within the French abbreviation

parts.note: in esse is Latin for in actual existence

explanation.surface: A trickster's hope is genuinely deceived by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a finesse tries to win a trick with a lower card, hoping the higher one lies with a particular opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attempting a finesse is staking a trick on the cards lying favourably.

clue.text: Some 19 that's extractable from tropical plants or shrubbery

definitions.meaning: 19 is the card game; a set of games of it, best of three, is a rubber
latex tapped from trees is made into elastic material

indicators.note: the word sits inside shrubbery as an alternative source

explanation.surface: A material obtainable from tropical plants or garden bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge match of best of three games is so called; the elastic latex product is the other sense.

clue.text: Handsome youth holding hand down bids in oddly deficient way

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are missing, leaving the even ones of these three words

explanation.surface: A good-looking lad, holding a hand, makes his bids badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis, beloved of Aphrodite in Greek myth, stands for any beautiful young man.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth's name is used for any very handsome young man.

clue.text: After top honour, duke worsted in court, in a way

definitions.text: worsted in court, in a way

indicators.note: the duke comes after the top card

parts.note: the ace is the highest of the honour cards

explanation.surface: After the top card, a duke was beaten in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is a tennis court, not a law court: serving an ace beats the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving an unreturnable ball beats an opponent, one way of defeating them on a tennis court.

clue.text: Hard to handle, like a pointless holding?

definitions.meaning: unruly, not easily told what to do
a hand with no high-card points gives no grounds for a bid

explanation.surface: An unruly thing, like an asset with no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly people will not do as bidden; a hand without points is too weak to bid on.

clue.text: Positive indicators about right requirements for contract

indicators.note: the marks surround the abbreviation

parts.note: ticks mark correct answers

explanation.surface: Approving marks around the right conditions for an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the contract is the number of tricks the declarer promises to make.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge contract is fulfilled by winning a stated number of rounds of play.

clue.text: Bid one's spades over West, showing immaturity

parts.note: a call is any bid in bridge

indicators.note: over in the sense of covering, so these letters go round the compass point

parts.note: one's gives ONES, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A bidder calls spades over West's head and looks green.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of experience and youthful rawness is the sense of inexperience shown.

clue.text: Difficult partner no longer playing

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
acting is playing a role

explanation.surface: A tricky former partner who has stopped performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding task is hard work, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Claim about line with ace and queen that's made by professional

indicators.note: the claim is wrapped round the other letters

parts.note: to say is to claim or assert
A is the abbreviation for ace on cards
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A player claims a trick with ace and queen, as a pro would.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional earns a fixed monthly or yearly wage, which is what is made.

clue.text: Penalties for players, not clubs

definitions.meaning: in football a referee sends a player off with a scarlet card
hearts and diamonds are the scarlet suits, unlike black clubs

explanation.surface: Punishments for sportsmen who are not members of clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Football referees show a scarlet card for a sending-off; hearts and diamonds are scarlet suits, clubs black.

clue.text: Don't follow suit — change to green energy

indicators.note: the letters of green plus the symbol are altered into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Stop copying others and switch to renewable power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow suit' sounds like imitation, but in cards it means playing the suit led; failing to when able is the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, failing to play the led suit despite holding it is the technical offence.

clue.text: Blow to West coming from unwise bid, ultimately, since double goes in

indicators.note: the two words are placed inside the pair of final letters
the final letters of each of the two words are taken

parts.note: as means since, because
a twin is a double, an exact copy

explanation.surface: A setback for West results from an unwise bid, since a double is put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a setback; it is the verb for wind blowing, and an east wind blows towards the west.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the east blows westward, so it is a blow travelling in that direction.

clue.text: Part of 6 or 24 down for English composer

definitions.meaning: both the stringed instrument at 6 and the facial feature at 24 have a raised ridge called by this name
Frank ..., English composer and Britten's teacher

explanation.surface: A piece of a fiddle or a nose belongs to an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The violin's string support and the nose's upper ridge share the name; Frank Bridge wrote music.

clue.text: Complaint I had rejected — more upset about diamonds

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the contraction is reversed

parts.note: I'd, contracted, gives ID

indicators.note: the comparative is wrapped round the suit letter

parts.note: sorer means more aggrieved

explanation.surface: A grumble: I had turned down diamonds and grew more annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment or illness is a medical complaint, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Way to dramatically expose king not ruled out

definitions.meaning: Hamlet stages a drama to catch the conscience of the king, Claudius
a ball still live, within the field of play

explanation.surface: A method for theatrically unmasking a monarch, still possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet exposes Claudius by means of a staged drama; a ball still live is said to be so.

clue.text: Defend against South, in another test for learner

indicators.note: the compass letter goes inside the exam word

parts.note: a resit is a second sitting of an exam

explanation.surface: South defends in a second exam a student must take.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand an attack is to fight back against it, the verb's basic sense.

clue.text: Leader's odd new arrangement of pack

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the word Leader is rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: The leader's peculiar shuffle of the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing the cards out again gives a fresh distribution of the deck.

clue.text: Made first bid, holding cards tight? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the bidding word wraps round the cards

parts.note: in bridge, to open is to make the first bid
a hand is the cards a player holds

explanation.surface: An opening bidder clutches their cards closely, or rather does the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' means stingy, and the opposite is generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous people are free with money, the reverse of tight-fisted meanness.

clue.text: Reports from one couple at table about another

indicators.note: the first pair goes round the second

parts.note: North and South form one partnership at a bridge table
East and West form the other partnership

explanation.surface: Gossip from one pair of players about the other pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge partnerships are North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events are what a bulletin carries, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Advance cautiously, finishing in two hearts, vulnerable

indicators.note: the closing letters of the following four words are taken

explanation.surface: Bid cautiously, ending in two hearts while vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a vulnerable side faces larger penalties, hence caution.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward carefully, as a car into traffic, is the verb sense meant.

clue.text: Didn't bid spades, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the word spades is rearranged

explanation.surface: A player failed to bid spades, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining to bid at bridge is said to be a pass, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Turn of partner to err — for example, about passing

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes round the other letters
turn means the word pal is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a partner or friend
to sin is to err

explanation.surface: A partner's turn to make a mistake, with talk about passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of' reads as a player's go at the table, but it signals a reversal of the partner word; 'about' wraps the example abbreviation round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Time going by is the sense meant: as time goes it slips away.
